headline: Computers don't think—they follow instructions billions of times per second
universal_truth: Speed and reliability can substitute for intelligence; simple rules executed fast produce complex results
fun_facts: Modern processors execute billions of operations per second—each one simple, but together powerful
All computer operations reduce to combinations of just three logical gates: AND, OR, and NOT
Your smartphone is millions of times more powerful than the computers that guided Apollo to the moon
discussion_questions: Do computers 'think' in any meaningful sense?
What can computers do that humans can't? What can't they do?
How has computing changed what's possible?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: Computers seem intelligent—they beat chess champions and translate languages. But they don't think like you. They follow instructions, billions per second, with perfect reliability. Speed and precision create an illusion of intelligence.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: If computers just follow instructions, how do they do things that seem to require understanding—like recognizing faces or writing text? Where does the apparent intelligence come from?
cliff.prompt: How do simple instructions produce intelligent-seeming results?

options.text: Massive speed and the right algorithms can mimic intelligence without understanding
options.response: Yes. A billion simple operations per second, well-organized, produces results that seem intelligent—even without true understanding.

options.text: Modern computers have developed a form of artificial understanding
options.response: This is debated, but computers still fundamentally execute instructions—very fast and very reliably...

q1.title: Binary Foundation
q1.script: Computers work in binary—just ones and zeros, on and off. Every image, song, and document reduces to these two states. From this simplicity emerges all complexity. Computers prove that enough simple pieces can create anything.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Binary Foundation"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Three Gates
q2.script: All computer logic reduces to three operations: AND, OR, and NOT. That's it. From these three building blocks, you can construct any computation. Universal machines from trivial parts. Simplicity can generate infinite complexity.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Speed Advantage
q3.script: Modern chips execute billions of operations per second. A calculation that would take you years happens in milliseconds. This speed advantage—not superior thinking—is why computers outperform humans at many tasks.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Speed and reliability can substitute for intelligence. Computers teach that simple rules executed very fast can produce astonishing results. The magic is in scale and precision, not in thinking.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 117. Tomorrow, we'll discover what robots can do. Until then, consider that your devices run on binary simplicity executed at impossible speed.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Computation Appreciation - See the Speed
growTrack.learning_objective: Appreciate the scale of computer operations
growTrack.activity: Think about something your computer does instantly—loading a webpage, searching files. Estimate how long it would take you to do manually. The gap between human speed and computer speed is almost inconceivable. That gap is their power.
